data.title: NFC Relay Geographic Impossibility on Contactless Transaction
data.description: Detects contactless (tap-to-pay) transactions where the POS terminal location is geographically impossible given the cardholder's last known location. When a contactless transaction occurs at a POS terminal more than 100 kilometers from the cardholder's most recent authenticated activity (mobile banking login, ATM withdrawal, or prior in-person transaction) within a timeframe that makes physical travel impossible, it indicates NFC relay (ghost-tapping) or unauthorized wallet token use. This rule specifically targets the Phase 4 execution stage of digital wallet fraud and NFC relay attacks (TP-0037), where money mules conduct contactless purchases using relayed card data at POS terminals geographically distant from the legitimate cardholder.

detection.condition: selection and correlation_geographic and filter_distance and filter_travel_impossible

enrichment_required.source: Geolocation enrichment (geodesic distance calculation between IP geolocations)
Geolocation enrichment (travel speed calculation between login locations)

falsepositives: Cardholders who travel by air and conduct transactions shortly after landing
Corporate cards used by multiple authorized individuals in different locations
Mobile banking geolocation errors due to VPN or proxy usage
